newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-GOUGH FINISHES WITH CAREER-BEST FIGURES IN ENGLAND VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOUGH FINISHES WITH CAREER-BEST FIGURES IN ENGLAND VICTORY.

text.p: Darren Gough bowled England to a morale boosting 115-run victory on the final day of their match against Matabeleland on Friday.
The Yorkshire paceman finished with five for 75, to end the match with a career best return of 11 for 139, as Matabeleland were bowled out for 261.
England, who have had a poor start to the tour, clinched their victory with 11 overs to spare in the final hour.
Mike Atherton's team meet Zimbabwe in the first of three one-day internationals in Bulawayo on Sunday.
Gough made two early breakthroughs to reduce the hosts to 20 for two and then returned in the final session with the second new ball to wrap up the tail.
In between a century by opening batsman Mark Dekker held up England's progress and briefly threatened to save the game.
Dekker added 156 for the third wicket with Zimbabwe all-rounder Heath Streak and while they were at the wicket there were even remote thoughts that Matabeleland might reach the victory target of 377.
But Streak's dismissal signalled a collapse that saw five wickets fall for 28 runs. Streak was bowled by Andy Caddick for 67, made from 143 balls with nine boundaries.

Dekker swept three sixes off spinners Robert Croft and Phil Tufnell but slowed down in the 90s. He was eventually trapped lbw by the deserving Croft for 104, made from 213 balls with three sixes and six fours.
The return of Gough in the evening sunshine hastened a welcome victory for the touringteam. He produced quick, full-length deliveries to bowl Andy Whittall and Henry Olonga.
Croft took the final wicket to finish with five for 65.
